arxiv-1908-01622.description: Abstract The High School Project on Astrophysics Research with Cosmics (HiSPARC) is a large extensive air shower (EAS) array with detection stations throughout the Netherlands, United Kingdom, Denmark and Namibia. HiSPARC is a collaboration of universities, scientific institutes and high schools. The majority of detection stations is hosted by high schools.

arxiv-2101-02766.creator: Han-Ching Ou, Haipeng Chen, Shahin Jabbari and Milind Tambe
arxiv-2101-02766.description: Abstract . Active screening is a common approach in controlling the spread of recurring infectious diseases such as tuberculosis and influenza. In this approach, health workers periodically select a subset of population for screening. However, given the limited number of health workers, only a small subset of the population can be visited in any given time period.

arxiv-2103-07774.title: Tykhonov Well-posedness of a Heat Transfer Problem with Unilateral Constraints
arxiv-2103-07774.creator: Mircea Sofonea, Perpignan, Domingo A. Tarzia, Rosario
arxiv-2103-07774.description: Abstract Abstract. We consider an elliptic boundary value problem with unilateral constraints and subdifferential boundary conditions. The problem describes the heat transfer in a domain D\subset{{\rm I}\mkern-3.0mu{\rm R}}^{d} and its weak formulation is in the form of a hemivariational inequality for the temperature field, denoted by {\cal P} .

arxiv-2111-14807.title: On formally undecidable propositions in nondeterministic languages
arxiv-2111-14807.creator: Martin Kolář
arxiv-2111-14807.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Martin Kolář. Any class of languages 𝐋 \mathbf{L} accepted in time 𝐓 \mathbf{T} has a counterpart 𝐍𝐋 \mathbf{NL} accepted in nondeterministic time 𝐍𝐓 \mathbf{NT} . It follows from the definition of nondeterministic languages that 𝐋 ⊆ 𝐍𝐋 \mathbf{L}\subseteq\mathbf{NL} . This work shows that every sufficiently powerful language in 𝐋 \mathbf{L} contains a string corresponding to Gödel’s undecidable proposition, but this string is not contained in its nondeterministic counterpart.

arxiv-2201-11273.title: On the category of structure species
arxiv-2201-11273.creator: Yasuhiro Wakabayashi
arxiv-2201-11273.description: Abstract . The purpose of the present paper is to make a mathematical study of the differences and relations among possible structures inherent in an object, as well as of the whole structure constituted by them (i.e., the structure of structures), against the background of the structuralism by Claude Lévi-Strauss and others.

arxiv-2208-02610.title: Twitter Attribute Classification with Q-Learning on Bitcoin Price Prediction Thanks: ∗ Corresponding author. School of Computing, Gachon University, Republic of Korea. (email: jychoi19@gachon.ac.kr)
arxiv-2208-02610.creator: Sattarov Otabek, Jaeyoung Choi
arxiv-2208-02610.description: Abstract Bitcoin price prediction based on people’s opinions on Twitter usually requires millions of tweets, using different text mining techniques, and developing a machine learning model to perform the prediction. These attempts lead to the employment of a significant amount of computer power, central processing unit (CPU) utilization, random-access memory (RAM) usage, and time.

arxiv-2210-14728.title: On a Class of Non-linear Differential Equations Arising from Branching Diffusions
arxiv-2210-14728.description: Abstract A non-linear differential equation arising from a stochastic process known as branching Brownian motion is considered. We find an explicit solution and show the uniqueness of the solution under some boundedness conditions using probabilistic ideas. We discuss non-negative solutions. We also generalize this idea to a class of non-linear parabolic differential equations which we call probabilistic parabolic equations.

arxiv-2303-16208.title: Lifting uniform learners via distributional decomposition
arxiv-2303-16208.creator: Guy Blanc, Jane Lange, Ali Malik, Li-Yang Tan
arxiv-2303-16208.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Guy Blanc, Jane Lange, Ali Malik, Li-Yang Tan. We show how any PAC learning algorithm that works under the uniform distribution can be transformed, in a blackbox fashion, into one that works under an arbitrary and unknown distribution 𝒟 \mathcal{D} .

arxiv-2304-05135.description: Abstract . Federated learning (FL) provides a variety of privacy advantages by allowing clients to collaboratively train a model without sharing their private data. However, recent studies have shown that private information can still be leaked through shared gradients. To further minimize the risk of privacy leakage, existing defenses usually require clients to locally modify their gradients (e.g.

arxiv-2309-05075.title: Secure Set-Based State Estimation for Linear Systems under Adversarial Attacks on Sensors Thanks: This work is supported by the Swedish Research Council and the Knut and Alice Wallenberg Foundation, Sweden. It has also received funding from the European Union’s Horizon Research and Innovation Progra
arxiv-2309-05075.creator: M. Umar B. Niazi, Michelle S. Chong, Amr Alanwar, Karl H. Johansson
arxiv-2309-05075.description: Abstract Set-based state estimation plays a vital role in the safety verification of dynamical systems, which becomes significantly challenging when the system’s sensors are susceptible to cyber-attacks. Existing methods often impose limitations on the attacker’s capabilities, restricting the number of attacked sensors to be strictly less than half of the total number of sensors.

arxiv-2310-13078.title: Imaging of X-ray Pairs in a Spontaneous Parametric Down-Conversion Process
arxiv-2310-13078.creator: Justin C. Goodrich, Ryan Mahon, Joseph Hanrahan, Monika Dziubelski, Raphael A. Abrahao, Sanjit Karmakar, Kazimierz J. Gofron, Thomas Caswell, Daniel Allan, Lonny Berman, Andrei Fluerasu, Andrei Nomerotski, Cinzia DaVià, Sean McSweeney
arxiv-2310-13078.description: Abstract Spontaneous parametric down-conversion is a vital method for generating correlated photon pairs in the visible and near-infrared spectral regions; however, its extension to X-ray frequencies has faced substantial barriers. Here, we present an advancement in correlated X-ray pair generation and detection by employing a two-dimensional pixelated detector to obtain the first direct image of the pair distribution.

arxiv-2310-14404.title: Be Selfish, But Wisely: Investigating the Impact of Agent Personality in Mixed-Motive Human-Agent Interactions
arxiv-2310-14404.creator: Kushal Chawla Ian Wu Yu Rong Gale M. Lucas Jonathan GratchUniversity of Southern California, Los Angeles, USA
arxiv-2310-14404.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Kushal Chawla Ian Wu Yu Rong Gale M. Lucas Jonathan GratchUniversity of Southern California, Los Angeles, USA. A natural way to design a negotiation dialogue system is via self-play RL: train an agent that learns to maximize its performance by interacting with a simulated user that has been designed to imitate human-human dialogue data.

arxiv-2402-06005.title: The Almost Sure Evolution of Hierarchy Among Similar Competitors
arxiv-2402-06005.creator: Christopher Cebra, Alexander Strang
arxiv-2402-06005.description: Abstract While generic competitive systems exhibit mixtures of hierarchy and cycles, real-world systems are predominantly hierarchical. We demonstrate and extend a mechanism for hierarchy; systems with similar agents approach perfect hierarchy in expectation. A variety of evolutionary mechanisms plausibly select for nearly homogeneous populations, however, extant work does not explicitly link selection dynamics to hierarchy formation via population concentration.

arxiv-2404-12169.title: Shotit: compute-efficient image-to-video search engine for the cloud Conference: ; ;
arxiv-2404-12169.creator: Leslie Wong
arxiv-2404-12169.description: Abstract . With the rapid growth of information technology, users are exposed to a massive amount of data online, including image, music, and video. This has led to strong needs to provide effective corresponsive search services such as image, music, and video search services.

arxiv-2502-20978.title: Using quantile time series and historical simulation to forecast financial risk multiple steps ahead
arxiv-2502-20978.creator: Richard Gerlach, Antonio Naimoli, Giuseppe Storti
arxiv-2502-20978.description: Abstract A method for quantile-based, semi-parametric historical simulation estimation of multiple step ahead Value-at-Risk (VaR) and Expected Shortfall (ES) models is developed. It uses the quantile loss function, analogous to how the quasi-likelihood is employed by standard historical simulation methods.

arxiv-2504-20019.title: Modelling of Underwater Vehicles using Physics-Informed Neural Networks with Control Thanks: This research was partially supported by the Aarhus University Research Foundation, EIVA a/s and Innovation Fund Denmark under grant 2040-00032B. Thanks: ∗ These authors contributed equally to this work.
arxiv-2504-20019.creator: Abdelhakim Amer ∗, David Felsager ∗, Yury Brodskiy, Andriy Sarabakha
arxiv-2504-20019.description: Abstract Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) integrate physical laws with data-driven models to improve generalization and sample efficiency. This work introduces an open-source implementation of the Physics-Informed Neural Network with Control (PINC) framework, designed to model the dynamics of an underwater vehicle.

arxiv-2508-14166.title: Testing the dark side of neutrino oscillations with the solar neutrino fog at Dark Matter experiments
arxiv-2508-14166.creator: Julia Gehrlein, Tanmay Kushwaha
arxiv-2508-14166.description: Abstract The recent detection of the solar neutrino background at Dark Matter direct detection experiments paves the way to fully explore an important degeneracy in neutrino oscillations in the presence of new interactions, named the LMA-Dark degeneracy. This degeneracy makes it impossible to determine the neutrino mass ordering in oscillation experiments if neutrinos have new vectorial interactions with matter.

arxiv-2509-09705.title: The Non-Determinism of Small LLMs: Evidence of Low Answer Consistency in Repetition Trials of Standard Multiple-Choice Benchmarks
arxiv-2509-09705.creator: Claudio Pinhanez, Paulo Cavalin, Cassia Sanctos, Marcelo Grave, Yago Primerano
arxiv-2509-09705.description: Abstract This work explores the consistency of small LLMs (2B-8B parameters) in answering multiple times the same question. We present a study on known, open-source LLMs responding to 10 repetitions of questions from the multiple-choice benchmarks MMLU-Redux and MedQA, considering different inference temperatures, small vs. medium models (50B-80B), finetuned vs. base models, and other parameters.

arxiv-2601-03591.title: Interplay of activity and non-reciprocity in tracer dynamics: From non-equilibrium fluctuation-dissipation to giant diffusion
arxiv-2601-03591.creator: Subhajit Paul, Debasish Chaudhuri
arxiv-2601-03591.description: Abstract Non-reciprocal interactions play a key role in shaping transport in active and passive systems, giving rise to striking nonequilibrium behavior. Here, we study the dynamics of a tracer – active or passive – embedded in a bath of active or passive particles, coupled through non-reciprocal interactions.

arxiv-2601-07674.title: Self-Creating Random Walks for Decentralized Learning under Pac-Man Attacks
arxiv-2601-07674.creator: Xingran Chen 1, Parimal Parag 2, Rohit Bhagat 1, Salim El Rouayheb 1
arxiv-2601-07674.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Xingran Chen 1, Parimal Parag 2, Rohit Bhagat 1, Salim El Rouayheb 1. Random walk (RW)-based algorithms have long been popular in distributed systems due to low overheads and scalability, with recent growing applications in decentralized learning. However, their reliance on local interactions makes them inherently vulnerable to malicious behavior. In this work, we investigate an adversarial threat that we term the “Pac-Man” attack, in which a malicious node probabilistically terminates any RW that visits it.

pmc-10595655.title: Comparison of the Choices criteria with national logo criteria in Sweden and Singapore
pmc-10595655.creator: G Tognon, C Lee, W K Chan, A Ingman, M Wasserman, M Hunsberger, L Lissner, J Middelham, AJC Roodenburg, H Smorenburg
pmc-10595655.description: BackgroundFood-based dietary guidelines often do not consider processed food products and typically do not address the rising popularity of plant-based meat and dairy alternatives or non-nutritive sweeteners. Multi-level nutrient profiling systems, such as the Choices 5-level criteria, can surmount these limitations and support nutrition policies, including the development and enhancement of national front-of-pack labeling systems.

pmc-10597143.title: Virtual Reality simulation training improves health professionals’ knowledge in STEMI critical care
pmc-10597143.creator: S Licata, L Deroma, C Fresco, A Di Chiara
pmc-10597143.description: BackgroundIn Friuli-Venezia Giulia (FVG, Italy, 1.2M inhabitants), the STEMI network has been implemented with a regional educational programme since 2018. However, each step leading to a fast-track reperfusion needs specific interactions between critical care teams on the scene and in hospital that theoretical training cannot provide.

pmc-10608289.title: A Comprehensive Study of Techniques to Optimize the Extraction of Lipids from the Autotrophic Strain of the Microalgae Chlorella vulgaris
pmc-10608289.creator: Ian Foerster, Wayne Seames, Jasmine Oleksik, Alena Kubatova, Andrew Ross
pmc-10608289.description: Microalgae represent a promising source of triglycerides and free fatty acids, synthesized in the form of lipids, for use in renewable fuels and chemicals. One challenge is the ability to efficiently recover the lipids from within the microalgae cell. Although various techniques have been studied individually, a comprehensive study of extraction techniques using consistent experimental and analytical methodology is missing.

pmc-11442059.title: Predator perception of aposematic and cryptic color morphs in two Oophaga species
pmc-11442059.creator: Vasiliki Mantzana‐Oikonomaki, Ariel Rodríguez, Giselle Castillo‐Tamayo, Roberto Ibáñez, Heike Pröhl
pmc-11442059.description: Animals that are toxic often advertise their unprofitability to potential predators through bright aposematic colors while cryptic ones blend in with their natural background to avoid predators. In the poison dart frogs, Oophaga pumilio and O. granulifera, some populations in Costa Rica and Panama display cryptic green and aposematic red color morphs.

pmc-11451929.title: Current opinion: antiretrovirals during pregnancy and breastfeeding
pmc-11451929.creator: Laura Nijboer, Lena van der Wekken-Pas, Karoline Aebi-Popp, Elisabeth van Leeuwen, Angela Colbers
pmc-11451929.description: Purpose of reviewTo review the most important literature from the past 2 years on the pharmacokinetics of antiretrovirals in pregnancy, placental transfer, and breastmilk.Recent findingsConcentrations of antiretrovirals frequently used in pregnancy and their placental transfer are described, together with infant exposure through breastmilk. Also, applications of ex-vivo and in-silico studies, such as placenta perfusion studies and PBPK models, are discussed.

pmc-11600356.title: ZFYVE19 gene mutation: A novel variant of progressive familial intrahepatic cholestasis
pmc-11600356.creator: Dalal Ben Sabbahia, Meriem Atrasssi, Nissrine Bennani, Abdelhakim Benmoussa, Abdelhak Abkari
pmc-11600356.description: A recent nonsyndromic phenotype, newly linked to mutations in the ZFYVE19 gene, is characterized by the appearance of cholestasis accompanied by an increase in serum gamma‐glutamyltranspeptidase (GGT) from infancy or early childhood. Affected individuals generally present with hepatosplenomegaly and may develop portal hypertension.

pmc-11709631.title: Accuracy of intact performance on measures of odor identification, global cognition, and amyloid imaging for identifying lack of cognitive decline and dementia in the Mayo Clinic Study of Aging cohort
pmc-11709631.creator: Jeffrey N Motter, Seonjoo Lee, David S Knopman, Maria Vassilaki, Davangere Devanand
pmc-11709631.description: BackgroundPrevious studies have linked impaired odor identification and global cognition with increased risk of cognitive decline and transition to dementia. However, the reverse question remains: if individuals have intact performance on these measures, are they at reduced risk for transition?

pmc-12799574.title: Effects of Hibiscus sabdariffa calyx extract on IL-10, TNF-α, and woven bone during orthodontic relapse
pmc-12799574.creator: Evie L Pakpahan, Ida B Narmada, Retno P Rahayu
pmc-12799574.description: ObjectivesTooth relapse occurs after orthodontic treatment. Bioactive chemicals in Hibiscus sabdariffa calyx extract (HS-CE) can protect bones and prevent inflammation. This study evaluated the effects of HS-CE on interleukin-10 (IL-10), tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α) expression, and woven bone formation during orthodontic relapse.

pmc-12971813.title: Behavioral, antioxidant, and kynurenine pathway modulation of a specific strain of Ligilactobacillus salivarius in a preclinical model of depression
pmc-12971813.creator: David Martín-Hernández, Javier R. Caso, César Díaz-García, Pedro-Antonio Regidor, José Miguel Rizo, Marta Román, Rocío Gutiérrez, Juan Carlos Leza
pmc-12971813.description: PurposeCurrent antidepressants targeting neurotransmitters often fail to alleviate symptoms. Alternative hypotheses suggest inflammation may trigger an alternative route that converts tryptophan into kynurenine, reducing the bioavailability of tryptophan to synthesize serotonin while producing neuroactive metabolites such as quinolinic acid (QUINA, excitotoxic) and kynurenic acid (KYNA, neuroprotective).

pmc-13093954.title: Patterns and clusters of diet in relation to metabolic syndrome among adults in Ubungo (urban) and Kilindi (rural) districts, Tanzania: a cross-sectional study
pmc-13093954.creator: Linda S. Paulo, Gonçalo J. Piedade, Simeon Mayala, Vanessa Harris, Virissa C. Lenters, Daniel R. Mende, Appolinary Kamuhabwa, Gideon Kwesigabo, Folkert W. Asselbergs, Pilly Chillo, K. Klipstein-Grobusch
pmc-13093954.description: BackgroundThe prevalence of Metabolic Syndrome (MetS) is rising worldwide, with particularly high rates in regions undergoing rapid urbanization and dietary change, such as Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA). However, few studies have examined the relationship between dietary patterns, dietary clusters, and MetS in these transitioning communities.ObjectivesTo examine the associations between dietary patterns, dietary clusters, and MetS in urban and rural Tanzania.

pmc-13233608.title: Gender, indigeneity, and intersectional considerations; The mental health of frontline public safety and healthcare workers in Canada
pmc-13233608.creator: Lindsay P. Allen
pmc-13233608.description: IntroductionThere are high prevalences of PTSD and suicide in frontline professional emergency responders; currently in Canada, every two out of three of such frontline workers are suffering at least one mental disorder. Beyond individual psychoeducation, gender and intersectional considerations must be addressed to better support mental health of these workers.

pmc-13345787.title: Differences in coronary disease severity at time of acute coronary syndrome between Middle East and North America
pmc-13345787.creator: Firas J. Al Badarin, Ahmad Edris, Shahrukh Hashmani, Manpreet Kaur, Shashank Shekhar, Oshin Kanwar, Samir Kapadia, Emin Murat Tuzcu
pmc-13345787.description: Comparing angiographic findings of patients presenting with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) in the Middle East/Gulf (MEG) and North America (NA) may shed light onto how coronary artery disease (CAD) complexity at time of ACS presentation impacts immediate management and clinical outcomes. Therefore, we compared outcomes in concurrent ACS patients between MEG and NA.

pmc-13423203.title: Methicillin-Sensitive Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA) Bacteremia With Concomitant Prostatic and Panspinal Epidural Abscesses and Cerebral Infarcts: A Rare Presentation
pmc-13423203.creator: Muhammad Usman, Abdul Basit, Muhammad A Usman, Abdullah Saeed, Shahzaib Khaliq, Laiba Murtaza, Muhammad Zatmar Khan, Zarmina Bashir
pmc-13423203.description: Methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA) bacteremia is a severe bloodstream infection with potential for metastatic spread to multiple organs. Although prostatic abscesses are typically associated with gram-negative organisms, MSSA may rarely cause disseminated multisystem infection, particularly in patients with significant comorbidities. Early recognition and aggressive intervention are essential to improve outcomes.

pmc-13508287.title: Colon-targeting pH-responsive Bletilla striata polysaccharide coacervate microdroplets for ulcerative colitis therapy via macrophage reprogramming
pmc-13508287.creator: Qiantao Zhang, Lai Chai, Hui Liu, Xueer Hu, Yujing Niu, Hongli Cao, Xin Rao, Mingyuan Zhou, Yuchi Chen, Xiaoqing Ye, Fangmei Zhou, Zhishan Ding, Bingqi Zhu
pmc-13508287.description: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is an immune-mediated chronic inflammatory bowel disease that severely impairs patients’ quality of life. Efficient oral colon-targeted delivery systems are urgently needed to improve local therapeutic efficacy while minimizing systemic exposure. Herein, we developed a pH-responsive Eudragit S100-coated coacervate microdroplet system for the oral delivery of natural Bletilla striata polysaccharide (BSP), termed BSP@EU-Coac.

pmc-13538158.title: Genetic dissection of grain yield and correlated proxy traits under suboptimal conditions
pmc-13538158.creator: Yan-Cheng Lin, Claude Urbany, Antonina Shlykova, Armin C. Hölker, Milena Ouzunova, Thomas Presterl, Torsten Pook, Manfred Mayer, Sebastian Urzinger, Chris-Carolin Schön
pmc-13538158.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Key messageThis eight-founder MAGIC population represents a powerful resource for dissecting complex traits in maize, assessing the utility of drought proxy traits, and optimizing low-coverage whole-genome sequencing approaches.AbstractSecuring sustainable crop production requires the genetic improvement of abiotic stress tolerance. Due to the broad range of environmental factors causing abiotic stress and complex genotype-by-environment interactions, it is crucial to understand the genetic basis of crop yield under suboptimal conditions.

pmc-13582696.title: Prohedonic Emotion Regulation Goals in Everyday Life: How Increasing Positive Affect and Reducing Negative Affect Relate to the Emotion Regulation Process and Depression
pmc-13582696.creator: Alison B. Tuck, Gigi A. Taillon, Renee J. Thompson
pmc-13582696.description: Research finds that prohedonic emotion regulation (ER) plays a key role in psychological well-being. Despite prohedonic ER encompassing both increasing or maintaining positive affect (PA) and decreasing negative affect (NA), prohedonic ER is often examined without regard to these different forms.

pmc-13644545.title: Investigations of Intraoral Scan Body Extensions. Effect of Design on the Accuracy, Usability, and Feasibility for Digital Full‐Arch Implant Scans In Vitro
pmc-13644545.creator: Julian Hessel Baranowski, Michael Braian, Victoria Franke Stenport, Ann Wennerberg
pmc-13644545.description: ObjectivesTo evaluate the effect of different scan body extension designs on the accuracy, usability, and feasibility of digital full‐arch implant impressions in an edentulous mandibular model. Accuracy was expressed as trueness and precision, usability as scan time, and feasibility as the number of total scan failures.Material and MethodsAn edentulous mandibular model with four implants was fabricated with minimal surface morphology.
